This ignores existing bookings/calendar busy times on date-override days and can expose slots for hosts who are actually busy, allowing double bookings."

      "severity": "high",

      "title": "Multiple same-day date overrides are handled incorrectly",
      "body": "The date override logic uses dateOverrides.find where the callback returns true when the slot is outside that override. If a user has multiple overrides on the same date, the first override that does not contain the slot makes find return and the function returns false, even if a later override does contain the slot. Split overrides such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00 can therefore make all slots unavailable."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 117,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Slots overlapping the edge of a date override are treated as available",
      "body": "The override check only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. It does not require the whole slot to be inside the override. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is accepted. A slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because line 123 uses isAfter without also treating isSame(end) as outside. This can show slots where the fixed host is not fully available."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 114,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Day.js objects are compared with ===",
      "body": "The expression dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares object identity, not timestamp values, so it is always false. Any intended special handling for equal start/end overrides, such as a zero-length override marking unavailability, never runs."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 142,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours validation ignores the slot end time",
      "body": "In the working-hours check, end is computed from slotStartTime.hour() and slotStartTime.minute() instead of slotEndTime. The event length is therefore ignored when validating working hours, so a slot that starts within working hours but extends past workingHour.endTime is incorrectly considered available."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Working-hours validation is wrong for multiple intervals",
      "body": "The code uses workingHours.find and returns true, making the slot unavailable, if any working-hour interval on that day does not contain the slot. With multiple intervals in a day, a slot contained in one interval can be rejected because another interval does not contain it. The logic should verify that at least one interval fully contains the slot, or that no interval contains it."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 138,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Absence of working hours is treated as unrestricted availability",
      "body": "If workingHours is empty or has no entry whose days include the slot day, the find call returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check. For fixed hosts this can allow slots on days with no configured working hours, which defeats the purpose of enforcing fixed-host availability in round-robin events."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts",
      "line": 110,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Date override day comparison can use server-local timezone",
      "body": "dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(YYYY MM DD) formats in the server's local timezone, while slotStartTime is a UTC Day.js object. On a non-UTC server, an override near midnight may be matched to the wrong calendar date. The date should be normalized with .utc() before formatting."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 212,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "getSlots assumes optional override.timeZone is present",
      "body": "The new override conversion calls .tz(override.timeZone) for every active override, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and existing callers may provide date overrides without it. If override.timeZone is undefined, dayjs timezone behavior may fall back to the system timezone or fail, causing incorrect slot times or runtime errors. The code should require/validate timeZone or explicitly fall back to organizerTimeZone."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/lib/slots.ts",
      "line": 212,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Offset is calculated from Date.toString()",
      "body": "dayjs(override.start.toString()) parses the output of Date.prototype.toString, which is implementation/locale dependent and unnecessary. This can parse to a different instant than override.start in some environments. Use dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone) directly."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts",
      "line": 788,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Missing test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides",
      "body": "The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event with a date override in another timezone. There is no test creating a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and verifying that only slots where the fixed host is available are returned."
    }

findings.title: Date override check skips busy-time validation
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once a date override exists for the slot day (dateOverrideExist is true) and the slot is not rejected by the override predicate, the function returns true before reaching the busy.every(...) conflict check. This ignores existing bookings/calendar busy times on date-override days and can expose slots for hosts who are actually busy, allowing double bookings.

findings.title: Multiple same-day date overrides are handled incorrectly
findings.body: The date override logic uses dateOverrides.find where the callback returns true when the slot is outside that override. If a user has multiple overrides on the same date, the first override that does not contain the slot makes find return and the function returns false, even if a later override does contain the slot. Split overrides such as 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00 can therefore make all slots unavailable.

findings.title: Slots overlapping the edge of a date override are treated as available
findings.body: The override check only rejects slots that end at/before the override start or start after the override end. It does not require the whole slot to be inside the override. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it, or starts inside and ends after it, is accepted. A slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because line 123 uses isAfter without also treating isSame(end) as outside. This can show slots where the fixed host is not fully available.

findings.title: Day.js objects are compared with ===
findings.body: The expression dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) compares object identity, not timestamp values, so it is always false. Any intended special handling for equal start/end overrides, such as a zero-length override marking unavailability, never runs.

findings.title: Working-hours validation ignores the slot end time
findings.body: In the working-hours check, end is computed from slotStartTime.hour() and slotStartTime.minute() instead of slotEndTime. The event length is therefore ignored when validating working hours, so a slot that starts within working hours but extends past workingHour.endTime is incorrectly considered available.

findings.title: Working-hours validation is wrong for multiple intervals
findings.body: The code uses workingHours.find and returns true, making the slot unavailable, if any working-hour interval on that day does not contain the slot. With multiple intervals in a day, a slot contained in one interval can be rejected because another interval does not contain it. The logic should verify that at least one interval fully contains the slot, or that no interval contains it.

findings.title: Absence of working hours is treated as unrestricted availability
findings.body: If workingHours is empty or has no entry whose days include the slot day, the find call returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check. For fixed hosts this can allow slots on days with no configured working hours, which defeats the purpose of enforcing fixed-host availability in round-robin events.

findings.title: Date override day comparison can use server-local timezone
findings.body: dayjs(date.start).add(...).format(YYYY MM DD) formats in the server's local timezone, while slotStartTime is a UTC Day.js object. On a non-UTC server, an override near midnight may be matched to the wrong calendar date. The date should be normalized with .utc() before formatting.

findings.title: getSlots assumes optional override.timeZone is present
findings.body: The new override conversion calls .tz(override.timeZone) for every active override, but TimeRange.timeZone is optional and existing callers may provide date overrides without it. If override.timeZone is undefined, dayjs timezone behavior may fall back to the system timezone or fail, causing incorrect slot times or runtime errors. The code should require/validate timeZone or explicitly fall back to organizerTimeZone.

findings.title: Offset is calculated from Date.toString()
findings.body: dayjs(override.start.toString()) parses the output of Date.prototype.toString, which is implementation/locale dependent and unnecessary. This can parse to a different instant than override.start in some environments. Use dayjs(override.start).tz(override.timeZone) directly.

findings.title: Missing test for round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The PR description says it fixes date overrides for fixed hosts in round-robin events, but the added test only covers a personal event with a date override in another timezone. There is no test creating a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and verifying that only slots where the fixed host is available are returned.
